% Images: \includegraphics with the keys real documents use, the figure
% environment with a caption, and intrinsic sizing. The two fixtures beside
% this file are synthetic (see images-note.md) and 64x40 px at the default
% density, so their intrinsic size is 64pt x 40pt. Every image carries a
% text alternative — an alt key, or a caption that becomes one (WCAG 2.2
% SC 1.1.1; an image without either reports N0376).
\documentclass{article}
\usepackage{graphicx}

\begin{document}

\section{Figures}

An inline mark \includegraphics[height=8pt, alt={A small synthetic
mark}]{rects.png} sits in the line like a word.

\begin{center}
  \includegraphics[width=0.8\textwidth, alt={Three synthetic rectangles,
  wide}]{rects.png}
\end{center}

\begin{figure}
  \centering
  \includegraphics[width=3cm, height=3cm, keepaspectratio]{rects.jpg}
  \caption{Three rectangles, fitted}
\end{figure}

Scaled to half: \includegraphics[scale=0.5, alt={Three synthetic
rectangles, halved}]{rects.png}, and exactly sized:
\includegraphics[width=32pt, height=40pt, alt={Three synthetic rectangles,
squeezed}]{rects.png}.

A transparent overlay: \includegraphics[alt={Three synthetic rectangles
over transparency}]{rects-alpha.png} keeps its alpha.

\end{document}
